job.title: Director Transformation - City of Wanneroo
job.description:
About the City of Wanneroo

Home to more than 236,000 people, the City of Wanneroo is a young, diverse and rapidly growing community. With our population projected to grow by around 70% by 2046, we are actively planning for a future city of close to 500,000 residents.

From established suburbs and rapidly developing growth corridors to industrial precincts, coastal and rural communities and significant natural areas, our scale and diversity create exciting opportunities and complex challenges.

Our 1,000-plus employees are at the heart of delivering for this growing community. With a new Workforce Plan and Digital Strategy, we are investing in simpler systems and processes, better use of data and technology, and the organisational capability we will need for the decades ahead.

About the Position

Reporting directly to the CEO, the newly created Director Transformation will bring together digital, process and data transformation to shape a more scalable, efficient and effective organisation.

Leading around 70 FTE, you will align strategy, improvement, data and digital capability to drive whole-of-organisation change and deliver measurable value for our people and community.

You will also lead one of Council’s most visible commitments: providing 100% of transactional services online by 2030. This is a rare opportunity to build a new Directorate, shape its culture and capability, and leave a lasting imprint on one of Western Australia’s fastest-growing cities.

About you

We are looking for a values-driven, people-focused leader with a strong track record of enterprise-wide transformation, and the ability to bring people on the journey with you.

You will have led complex change, multidisciplinary projects and business improvement through to measurable outcomes, leaving both the organisation and your teams stronger as a result. You know how to simplify the way organisations work, build high-performing teams and turn ambitious targets into results.

If you are curious and collaborative, enjoy solving complex problems and genuinely get satisfaction from helping others do their best work, you will feel at home at the City of Wanneroo.

In Return

We are offering a contract of up to five-years, with a remuneration package of up to $330,821 per annum, comprising a base salary, superannuation (including the option to co-contribute up to 15%) and a vehicle or vehicle allowance.

We know that leaders do their best thinking when they are genuinely able to step away and recharge. This means you will receive five weeks’ annual leave, plus 12 executive leave days.

Most of all, you will join a leadership team that backs its people, welcomes fresh thinking, and is committed to making the City of Wanneroo a place where everyone can do their best work.

To apply, please click the Apply Now button or visit www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference 1132353. Please provide a comprehensive resume and a covering letter of no more than two pages, outlining your motivation for applying and addressing your suitability for the role.

Download an Application Pack here: https://beilbydt.com.au/application-packs

For initial enquiries, or for any assistance you may need in making your application, please contact Emily Bulloch for a confidential discussion on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au.

Applications close at 4pm AWST on Wednesday 14 October 2026.

Please note, canvassing of Elected Members will disqualify.

job.title: Senior Accounting Officer
job.description:
About WATC

As the State’s central financial services provider, Western Australian Treasury Corporation (WATC) cares about the financial health of Western Australia’s government sector. WATC partner with government entities to achieve sound financial outcomes and provide access to a comprehensive range of corporate finance, debt and investment, risk management and foreign exchange products and advisory services. They also provide their investors with secure and sustainable opportunities.

You can find out more about the organisation including our purpose, history and key activities by visiting the About Us tab on the WATC website.

The Opportunity
WATC are seeking an experienced Senior Accounting Officer to join their Finance, Administration and Treasury Operations team. Reporting to the Finance Manager, you will take ownership of accurate and timely financial accounting activities through to trial balance, including daily reconciliations and reporting that support WATC’s operations. This permanent role suits a self-managing professional who enjoys hands-on transactional accounting, works confidently to recurring deadlines, and is motivated to contribute to a high-performing team.
Key activities include:
  • Performing daily and month-end bank reconciliations and completing the daily profit and loss reconciliation process.
  • Managing accounts receivable activities, client accounting files and foreign currency invoice approvals.
  • Coordinating month-end processes, including journals, accruals, prepayments, balance sheet reconciliations and other financial adjustments.
  • Producing accurate monthly reporting through to a completed trial balance and supporting quarterly, statutory and management reporting.
  • Maintaining the integrity of the general ledger, chart of accounts, fixed asset register and supporting accounting systems and procedures.
  • Supporting tax compliance, year-end financial statements, internal and external audits, and the application of accounting standards.
  • Contributing ideas and practical improvements to processes, documentation and team initiatives.
About You

WATC’s ideal applicant is an organised and dependable accounting professional who combines strong technical capability with a practical, collaborative approach. You will be comfortable taking ownership of recurring daily deliverables, keeping stakeholders informed and maintaining accuracy during busy reporting periods.
If you can demonstrate the following capabilities and experience, we would love to hear from you:
  • CA or CPA qualification (or equivalent) with current membership.
  • Strong technical accounting knowledge, including the interpretation and application of Australian Accounting Standards.
  • Demonstrated experience in financial accounting, reconciliations and reporting through to trial balance.
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel skills and confidence using financial accounting and related business systems.
  • Ability to organise priorities, work autonomously and provide clear assurance that key deliverables are progressing.
  • Constructive and professional communication skills, with the confidence to work closely with the Finance Manager and a range of internal stakeholders.
  • A collaborative mindset, sound judgement and a genuine interest in improving efficiency, quality and productivity.
WATC Values

WATC values shape their behaviours and define how they relate to each other, their clients and their community:
Integrity – We are open, honest and accountable. We adhere to the highest professional and ethical standards. We honour our promises.
Partnership – We work collaboratively with our stakeholders and colleagues towards achieving successful outcomes.
Adaptability – We challenge ourselves to think creatively and to continuously improve.
Achievement – We are engaged and focused on delivering valued outcomes for Western Australia.
Leadership – We use our knowledge and experience to contribute to the long-term benefit of Western Australia.
Employee Benefits WATC offer a range of benefits beyond remuneration that include:
  • Flexible work arrangements:
    • A supportive approach to work / life balance
    • Working from home options and flexible start and finish times
    • Compressed work schedules and part-time work opportunities.
  • Health and wellbeing focus:
    • Calendar of a range of wellbeing initiatives
    • Two wellbeing days annually
    • Discounted health insurance.
  • Generous leave:
    • 12.5 days personal leave per year
    • Up to 12 weeks paid parental leave (on top of government paid parental leave scheme)
    • Access to purchase additional annual leave.
  • Diverse, inclusive and supportive work environment:
    • Strong organisational focus on diversity and inclusion
    • A reward and recognition program.
  • Professional development opportunities:
    • Professional memberships
    • Support for tertiary education.
  • Salary Packaging:
    • Novated lease for the purchase of a car
    • Salary packaging for personal IT equipment.
  • Contemporary offices:
    • Sit-stand desks and personal lockers
    • Free gym access and fitness classes in the building
    • Excellent end of trip facilities.
  
To find out more about the benefits of working at WATC, visit WATC’s Careers page.

How to Apply
WATC offer an inspiring and collaborative work environment where compliance is central to driving trust and innovation in financial services.
Join an organisation that is committed to employing highly skilled people, with diverse backgrounds and experiences that embraces diversity of all kinds including supporting Women In STEM.
You will have the opportunity to work within a supportive team that values excellence, transparency, and forward-thinking solutions. If you are seeking a role where you can make a tangible impact, apply now.

job.title: Central Services Manager

The Central Services Manager will lead the day-to-day delivery of the business support functions. Reporting to the Managing Director, you will oversee finance administration, people processes, systems, facilities, compliance and business development support.

This is a practical, hands-on role for someone who enjoys improving processes, supporting others and making sure important tasks are completed accurately and on time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee invoicing, accounts, payroll inputs, budgets and monthly reporting
  • Manage recruitment coordination, onboarding, employee records and other people processes
  • Maintain compliance, insurance, contracts, policies and business records
  • Coordinate IT support, systems, offices, equipment and key suppliers
  • Support CRM, opportunity tracking, marketing and bid coordination

  • Provide clear updates, recommendations and reports to the leadership team
About You

This role will suit an organised and commercially minded manager who is comfortable working across different business functions and getting involved in the detail when needed.

We would like to speak with candidates who can demonstrate:
  • Experience managing business operations or shared services in consulting, engineering, professional services or another project-based environment
  • Experience across areas such as people operations, compliance, contracts, systems, facilities or supplier management
  • Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • Confidence using Microsoft 365 and business systems
  • Clear communication, sound judgement and a reliable approach to follow-through

Based in the heart of Sydney CBD, this is a broad role where you can make a visible difference to how the business operates. You will work closely with senior leaders, improve the support available to technical teams and help build strong foundations for future growth.

job.title: Principal Assistant Energy and Water Ombudsman
job.description:
Lead a trusted, future-ready energy and water dispute resolution service: 5-year contract $250,000 salary package.

We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as the Traditional Custodians of this land. We recognise the continuing connection to land, waters, culture and community of all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. We pay our respects to their Elders past and present and recognise the strength, resilience and diversity of all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples across this land.

This is an exciting opportunity to join Ombudsman Western Australia as Principal Assistant Ombudsman, Energy and Water and play a key role in shaping the organisation's future. The position is offered as a five-year fixed-term appointment, with the possibility of extension.

About the Western Australian Ombudsman

The Parliamentary Commissioner for Administrative Investigations – more commonly known as the Ombudsman:
 
  • Protects People’s Rights: we give people a way to ensure they are heard when they feel they’ve been treated unfairly.
  • Improves Services and Build Trust in Government: we can investigate how services are delivered and bring weaknesses to the attention of decision-makers. In doing so, we improve service delivery for all Western Australians.
  • Prevents Harm: through death reviews, investigations and oversight of how organisations respond to allegations of child related harm, we identify opportunities to prevent deaths and strengthen the safety net around children.
  • Supports Vulnerable Communities: we can focus on people who are often overlooked or disadvantaged, ensuring their voices are heard and their needs are considered.
The Ombudsman also undertakes the role of the Energy and Water Ombudsman and is the Charitable Trusts Commissioner.

Staff of the Ombudsman’s Office

Our people are at the heart of the Ombudsman’s Office and central to its success. We are committed to supporting employees to grow and thrive through ongoing education, training and professional development opportunities. Flexible work arrangements may also be negotiated, helping employees balance their professional and personal commitments.

Equity and Diversity

The Ombudsman’s office provides services to a diverse range of people within the Western Australian community, and is committed to creating an equitable and diverse workforce. We encourage people with disabilities, people from culturally diverse backgrounds, and women and young people to apply. The office of the Ombudsman may prioritise recruitment decisions based on the Equal Opportunity Act Western Australia 1984 (EOA 1984).
The Ombudsman’s office is committed to growing the Aboriginal workforce. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply for this position under Section 51 of the EOA 1984 as a measure to achieve equality and increase workforce representation of Aboriginal people.
The position is covered by the Public Sector CSA Agreement 2024 and is located in the CBD, Perth Western Australia.

This Position

This is an opportunity to lead a respected independent service through an important period of change, with a clear mandate to modernise systems, improve data and insight capability, and strengthen EWOWA’s impact across Western Australia’s energy and water sectors.
EWOWA resolves disputes between individual and small business consumers and energy and water providers. The next phase calls for strategic leadership, service innovation, and the ability to turn insights into better practice and outcomes.
We are seeking an Executive Leader to strengthen EWOWA’s sustainability and grow a responsive, intelligence-led service that improves outcomes beyond individual complaints. Reporting to the Ombudsman and being very responsive to the Board, you will lead the Energy and Water Ombudsman function, advising the Board and key stakeholders, and helping EWOWA respond to emerging issues including climate resilience, energy transition, water infrastructure, affordability pressures and changing community expectations.
You will lead a capable team, promote a safe and inclusive culture, and build trusted relationships with regulators, industry, small business, consumer advocates, government agencies, and community organisations.
We are looking for someone who can:
  • Create an environment where people perform at their best.
  • Lead change and service improvement in operational processes.
  • Use data, intelligence, and engagement to achieve better outcomes.
  • Build credibility across government, industry, and community sectors.
  • Leverage customer service or dispute resolution experience to drive fairness.
  • Keep consumer needs central, including the needs of vulnerable and underrepresented communities throughout WA.
This role offers a rare opportunity to lead a service that supports Western Australians and drives better practice across the energy and water sectors. 
You will help ensure EWOWA remains trusted, effective, and future ready, while strengthening customer confidence in the Scheme’s accessibility and fairness.
All key responsibilities and selection criteria are outlined in the attached Job Description Form.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
The Company

This privately owned Western Australian business has built an outstanding reputation as a market leader in the design, manufacture and construction of customised industrial, commercial and rural infrastructure. With decades of success, a loyal client base and a strong pipeline of work, the company continues to experience sustainable growth across multiple sectors.

Known for delivering high-quality projects and exceptional customer service, the business combines strong family values with commercial discipline and is now seeking an experienced General Manager to work alongside the owners in leading the next phase of its evolution.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the owners, this is a broad executive leadership role with responsibility for the overall performance of the business. You'll lead a capable management team across operations, construction, sales, estimating, finance, customer service and business development, ensuring the organisation continues to grow profitably while maintaining the culture and reputation that has underpinned its long-term success.
This role offers genuine influence over both strategy and day-to-day operations, providing the opportunity to modernise systems, improve business performance and develop the next generation of leaders within the organisation.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide strategic and operational leadership across all areas of the business.
  • Lead, mentor and develop a high-performing leadership team.
  • Ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on time and profitably.
  • Support major tenders, commercial negotiations and business development initiatives.
  • Partner with the finance function on budgeting, forecasting, cash flow and profitability.
  • Strengthen business systems, technology platforms and operational processes.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across the organisation.
  • Build strong relationships with customers, suppliers, contractors and key stakeholders.
  • Monitor business performance and identify opportunities for sustainable growth.
  • Foster a positive, accountable and values-driven culture.
About You 

You are an experienced senior leader who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on operational leadership. You have successfully led multidisciplinary teams within construction, manufacturing, engineering or project-based businesses and understand how to drive both commercial performance and strong workplace culture.

You will also bring:
  • Proven executive leadership experience within construction, manufacturing, building products or a related industry.
  • Strong commercial, financial and operational management capability.
  • Experience leading sales, operations and project delivery functions.
  • Demonstrated success improving business systems and operational efficiency.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, negotiation and communication skills.
  • A collaborative leadership style with high emotional intelligence.
  • The ability to build trust, empower people and create accountability.
  • An ownership mindset with a genuine passion for growing successful businesses.
Why This Role

This is an outstanding opportunity to join an established and highly respected Western Australian business in a genuine leadership capacity. Working closely with the owners, you'll have the autonomy to shape strategy, influence business direction and make a lasting impact across every part of the organisation.

If you're looking for a role where you can combine commercial leadership with operational excellence in a stable, growing business, we'd welcome a confidential discussion.

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference number 1124188.  For initial enquiries or assistance with your application, please contact Nick Verkerk at nverkerk@beilbydt.com.au or Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Senior - Lead Design Engineer | Manager
job.description:

Responsibilities will include reviewing and allocating design enquiries, producing and approving calculations and drawings, supporting the sales team on major infrastructure projects, and developing the capability of design staff through training and mentoring.
  
About You
We are seeking a commercially minded engineering leader who has the following attributes:
  • Degree-qualified Civil, Structural or Mechanical Engineer, ideally CPEng and/or a member of Engineers Australia.
  • Proven experience leading engineering and design teams within construction, infrastructure, temporary works or related industries.
  • Strong technical understanding of formwork, shoring, falsework or scaffolding design and engineering principles.
  • Commercially minded, with the ability to develop safe, practical and cost-effective engineering solutions.

Why This Role

This is an exciting opportunity to lead an established engineering and design function, combining technical expertise, people leadership and commercial influence across major infrastructure and construction projects.

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via the “Apply for this job” button or through our website at www.beilbydt.com.au, quoting reference number 1129977. For further inquiries, please contact Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Director Community Planning and Development Services - Shire of Capel
job.description:
THE SHIRE

The Shire of Capel is a vibrant and connected community with a family-friendly lifestyle in the beautiful South-West region of Western Australia, situated between Bunbury and Busselton, in close proximity to the Margaret River region. The team embodies the Shire’s HEART values - honesty, empathy, accountability, respect and teamwork. This is a critical and exciting time for the Shire, with significant projects underway including a leadership and cultural development program and an ERP implementation, and the reshaping of the organisational structure including the creation of a third directorate, driven by the growth in the organisation.

THE ROLE

The Director Community, Planning & Development Services provides executive leadership for the following portfolios: community and economic development; libraries; planning and building services; and environmental health services. Reporting to the newly appointed CEO, you will be a key member of the Executive Leadership Team and contribute to the overall leadership, governance and performance of the organisation. A key focus of the role will be leading the development of the new Local Planning Scheme and shaping a clear vision to strengthen the Shire’s planning future.

REQUIREMENTS

If you are an accomplished senior leader with experience contributing to organisational strategy, governance and executive decision-making within a Local Government environment, we would be interested to hear from you. Significant experience in community development and strategic and statutory planning will be highly regarded, particularly where supported by a professional planning background. The successful candidate will also be an effective executive team member who can lead senior managers, build organisational capability and foster a strong culture of physical and psychosocial safety and customer service.

THE PACKAGE

An attractive remuneration package is on offer, including a base salary of $185,400 plus superannuation, a housing allowance of $26,000, a vehicle or vehicle allowance, and a professional development allowance, on a five-year contract.

For initial enquiries, or for any assistance you may need in making your application, please contact Emily Bulloch for a confidential discussion on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au.

job.title: Senior Project Development Engineer
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a major owner and operator of critical infrastructure supporting Australia's export supply chain. Operating a large-scale industrial asset base in Newcastle, the organisation is committed to safety, operational excellence and long-term asset stewardship.

With significant investment planned across its infrastructure portfolio, an opportunity has arisen for an experienced Senior Project Development Engineer to lead the identification, assessment and development of major capital and asset improvement initiatives.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Engineering Manager, you will lead the development of major engineering, maintenance and infrastructure projects from concept through to approval.

Working across Engineering, Maintenance, Commercial and Project Delivery teams, you will undertake feasibility studies, evaluate options, develop business cases, assess risk and prepare projects for successful execution.

You will manage multiple studies concurrently while providing strategic input into long-term asset planning, capital investment decisions and project prioritisation. The role offers regular engagement with senior leadership and the opportunity to influence significant infrastructure investment decisions.

About You

We are seeking an experienced engineer who combines strong technical capability with commercial insight and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Mechanical, Civil, Structural or related engineering
  • Experience within heavy industry, infrastructure, mining, manufacturing, logistics or asset intensive operations
  • Proven success in feasibility studies, project development and business case preparation
  • Strong understanding of project scope, cost, schedule and risk management
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities
  • Demonstrated commitment to safety, continuous improvement and operational excellence
Importantly, you will be recognised as a collaborative and solutions-focused professional who can build credibility across technical, operational and commercial teams while influencing positive outcomes and driving investment decisions.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to influence the future direction of a significant infrastructure asset portfolio and play a leading role in shaping major investment decisions. You will enjoy broad exposure across engineering, asset management, maintenance and project delivery disciplines while working on complex, high-value projects that directly impact long-term operational performance.

Offering both strategic influence and technical challenge, this role is ideally suited to an engineer who enjoys solving complex problems, engaging with senior stakeholders and developing projects from initial concept through to execution readiness. You'll join a business that values expertise, collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement, while providing the opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting contribution.

For a confidential discussion, contact Jessica O'Neill on 0457 336 833. Applications should be submitted via the apply now button.

job.title: Field Service Engineer

job.title: National Account Coordinator
job.description:
